content:
Dear everyone,
I'm not a mathematician, so i have no idea that my work have any relevance to anyone. However, lean allows me to be independent on me not knowing math. I'm playing with some hard problem, and on the way have proved with the help of another guy running llm to formalize my statement. Different llms says that the theorem is nontrivial (but I cannot judge). Apparently lean zulip is non friendly to people like me to ask whether the theorem have any relevance to any people. Should I just ignore it and hope that I can prove the interesting statement worth of publishing on arxiv? Being not mathematition i do not really care what field this theorem belongs to, so I'm not interested in finding right community and trying to fit community culture. Lean tells the theorem is correct and I'm fine with that.

PS. I was banned for posting announcement for the theorem for one day. I see no reason why people cannot use llm for the statement they cannot fully grasp, whereas llm provides the language that would be familiar to some other people.

Pps. I have a formalized proof of the statement that for any set of nonzero natural numbers {a_i} and any base n>=2 there exist a natural number k that the digit vectors of {k * a_i} written base n are linearly independent in the ring Z/Zn.

Llm says it is kind of derandomization of the common construction of, say, multiplicative hashes, and similar topics. Again I cannot judge. May be the theorem is trivial and there is no interest what so ever.

Ppps. If anyone need such theorem one can find it https://github.com/cacaomacao/Digit-vector-Independence

For moderators: I have formally asking a question whether community do not like people like me. In which case I would not bother you guys at all any more, but it is better if this statement would stay public, so that other people would not attempt to ask for intermediate results until the final picture is clear.

hi bro;) reading a page of virgin math papers makes me sleep, but I stay very focused when things get practical. I moved here from haskell because found hard to check logic encoded in type families. my goal is to verify miso-css library. I studied SF volumes 1 and 2, nng, leans.dev, and working on MIL. If agents are as good as their proponents say then the focus should shift from the proofs to specs

Hi Daniil, thanks for reply. I personally very inpatient and make huge number of mistakes when writing on paper or in code, so we have unique opportunity in lean to move programming in different paradigm. Instade of code verification one can do programming as a proof of specifications. The statement of theorem is a "function" signature, and the proof is the algorithm. No morere bugs. On top of the proof one can have a thin layer of translation to any programming language. I have started the project, but have very little resources to pursue it with the speed I want.

https://github.com/mkatkov/lean_c

That is combining sleeping math with practical world.

My current problem is to formalize complexity theory in a practical way, probably linking to big O notation to have complexity guaranty as a part of the specs proof.
